chunks.text:
technical — a heavily modified fork⁠ of Quartz⁠, hosted with Cloudflare Workers, with support for arXiv file pulling, telescopic text, custom homepage, a note view⁠, JSON Canvas support, Obsidian Bases support hierarchical grid layout, comment room support, reader view with custom folder and tags view, nested rss feed, Jupyter Notebooks support for client-side interaction, flashcards, health stuff, tufteThis is a tiny sidenote, supporting dynamic view size. Very much along the lines of Tufte CSS sidenotes, sidepanels 1, custom popover, modified Flexoki. I also host all of the LFS on Cloudflare R2, and have a middleware as a proxy client. There are also course workspaces, a PDF reader with marks and notes, a saved-link reading queue, browser semantic search, pronunciation tools, and a little mascot wandering around the page edges. The homepage has local weather and a shared walking trail. Also custom 404 page because why not. Oh, there’s also a Tractatus-specific layout, technical docs layout, french-specific layout, and more.Thanks to Opus and Astra for prototyping a lot of the mocks/ideas I have for these.
typography — PP Neue Montreal, Space Grotesk, Parclo Serif, ITC Garamond and berkeley mono
accessibility — native buttons, dialogs and popovers, keyboard navigation, visible focus, and ARIA labels for the controls that need them. The mascot and 404 landscape respect the reduced-motion preference. Press D outside text fields to cycle through daylight, system, dark, and light themes. Cmd/Ctrl+’ opens the shortcuts helper.
components — I added support for rendering tikz graph, pseudocode support, dynalist-inspired collapsible header, a few customised signature, tiny transformers plugins, micromarks extensions for wikilinks, sidenotes, protected notes, distributed comments, and additional supports of renderPage.tsx
usage — Some daily drivers that has found its way into my life. But I use Obsidian for note-taking and Apple Notes while I’m on the go, in conjunction with neovim⁠ for all my work-related shenanigans.
license — All my notes are licensed under CC BY-NC-SA 2, whilst the code is under Apache 2.0. Original authors are referenced and linked, and their work retains its own licenses. The note footer renders the Creative Commons marks.

For a more compact highlights, see this list
courses and lecture workspaces
I want to explore a spaced repetition interface for some of the OCW course. This include the lecture notes, alongside problem sets, and decks.
There are some video lecturesVideo lecture pages also pair with captions for better accessibility. For folks that enjoy latex, those are also imported to the linked study notes. that paired with backlinks that allows better graph navigation. I explicitly did not enable graph given that it creates too much cognitive overload (or at least for me whenever I look at a graph).
PDF reader
PDFs in the garden open in a reader with a document library, outline, page navigation, zoom, text selection, marks, and Markdown notes with math. It remembers reading position and can link directly to a page or mark. Course resource pages use the same reader, so their marks stay attached when opening the source beside a lecture. The original file remains available through the raw-file link.
feed
A reading queue combines links from are.na and curius, allowing me to go through all of the links backlog I have. There are also some custom parsing courtesy of defuddle
search
Search expands based on Quartz’ default lexical search, with semantic enabled. I used EmbeddingGemma 2 through Transformers.js and precompute the whole garden’s embeddings. Feel free to take a look at the RAG pipeline, pretty standard nowadays.
training
I use both Strava and TrainingPeaks, but triathlon page brings together Strava, Garmin, Wahoo, Oura, Apple Health, and CORE records with logs. Of course it has to have our own styling and preferences. There are a bunch of stuff to explore in terms of data analytics and exploration, with also activities that contains wind data, cycling CdA.
There are also a bunch of maths and sports physiology in there for maximize human-performance 😸 (i’m just a sucker for data, but it is all fun and game)
mascots
Very rudimentary hand-drawn mascot appears in the favicon, social cards, and page artwork. Its animated version perches on headings, code blocks, figures, and other page edges, then rides the scroll rail while the page moves. If you wish to turn the pets off, then press Ctrl+p (but Blob wouldn’t like that)

pronunciation and source text
French notes and decks have pronunciation controls with playback-speed settings. gv opens those settings. Audio uses cached clips when available and an optional browser speech model for synthesis. We use a speech models to support French and English.
The metadata row can copy a note’s Markdown source to the clipboard and reports whether the copy succeeded. Appending .md to a note URL also serves the source. Notebook cells, mathematical diagrams, and slide views have their own interactive rendering, including numbered slide pages and an overview grid.

Supports Bases API and JSON Canvas
Bases render tables, lists, image galleries, maps, and Kanban columns. The film analysis view uses the first studio entry as the main production company and places each film in one column. This convention is saved as a Bases formula; notes keep their full list of production companies. Obsidian can show those lists as combined group labels. Search filters cards and updates column counts. The .base file controls filters, sorting, visible properties, image fit, and column width; note creation and property edits happen in Obsidian.

```pseudo
\begin{algorithm}
\caption{LLM token sampling}
\begin{algorithmic}
\Function{sample}{$L$}
\State $s \gets ()$
\For{$i \gets 1, L$}
\State $\alpha \gets \text{LM}(s, \theta)$
\State Sample $w \sim \text{Categorical}(\alpha)$
\If{$w = \text{EOS}$}
\State \textbf{break}
\EndIf
\State $s \gets \operatorname{append}(s, w)$
\EndFor
\State \Return $s$
\EndFunction
\end{algorithmic}
\end{algorithm}
```

flashcards
credit to eudoxia0/hashcards. Check out an example set of flashcards on sets theory. Decks support question/answer and cloze cards, math, and stable card identities. The source note can sit beside the active card, and a course review combines due cards from its decks. Signed-in owner reviews use FSRS, with saved review history and undo. Grading a cloze card defers its siblings until the next session.
